content:
anna: Heads-up — during the canary for dedicated-gpu we started seeing deploy jobs succeed but the GPU tasks fail with 403 when trying to read model artifacts and KMS decrypts show permission denied. :grimacing:
anna: Paste of the error from node logs:
anna: ```
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z ERROR runtime fetch: failed to decrypt: googleapis.com/kms.decrypt denied for serviceaccount:deploy-runner@project.
kubelet: failed to pull secret: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor not permitted
```
devon: ack — did anything change to the deploy SA bindings this morning? @raj any RBAC rollouts? :eyes:
raj: We shipped the least-privilege rollout at 09:30 — converted a couple of clusterrolebindings for deploys into namespace-scoped rolebindings. That should be fine, but maybe the KMS IAM linkage is using impersonation requiring actAs?
anna: I dug into audit logs and there's an odd pattern: the KMS decrypt entries are being filtered out in our sink for a subset of namespaces. auditd-bot posted a dropped-log event at 14:13.
auditd-bot: Dropped 47 events matching filter: severity<INFO and source!=control-plane — rule triggered for ns=different-tenant.
devon: oh no. So not only RBAC change but also our audit sink suppression hid the failures initially. That's why SRE saw the deploy as OK.
raj: Can you paste the rolebinding for the deploy-runner SA in the gpu namespace?
anna: ```
$ kubectl -n gpu get rolebinding deploy-runner-binding -o yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: deploy-runner-binding
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy-runner
  namespace: gpu
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: deploy-runner-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
anna: role has permissions to get/secrets but not to impersonate other service accounts. our KMS integration uses workload identity and requires iam.serviceAccounts.get + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the GCP side for the SA that the workload impersonates.
devon: Right — earlier we were using a cluster-level binding that allowed actAs via a dedicated iam-binding. The refactor moved the permission into a namespace-scoped binding but the GCP IAM grant was left referencing the old SA path.
raj: Proposed mitigation: re-add minimal iam.roles/iam.serviceAccountUser actAs for the specific workload SA, scoped to the deploy-runner SA only. Also temporarily relax audit sink filter to surface the missing decrypts so we can validate.
sre-oncall: I'm going to patch the audit sink now (rolling to verbose for the gpu ns) and create an alert rule for kms.decrypt denied.
ops-bot: Runbook snippet triggered: "If KMS decrypt denied for service account during deploy, check GCP IAM binding for service account impersonation and corresponding Kubernetes RoleBinding."
anna: I applied a narrow iam binding for serviceAccount:project.svc.id.goog[gpu/deploy-runner] -> roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on the decryptor SA. Re-triggering canary.
raj: Also add a small e2e that attempts a KMS decrypt via the mounted SA token so we don't regress during RBAC refactors.
devon: After the patch can you confirm logs show successful decrypts? If green, we need a postmortem with action items: (1) gating checklist for RBAC refactors, (2) automated KMS test, (3) audit sink coverage test, (4) owner for deploy SA iam mapping.
anna: Initial canary logs: success! ```2026-03-18T14:21:10Z INFO kms: decrypt OK for job gpu-canary-7``` :tada:
raj: Nice. I'll draft the short postmortem and include the exact terraform diff to reintroduce the narrow iam binding. Also adding a unit test in infra-ci that validates the deploy-runner cancallable KMS decrypts.
sre-oncall: Filing incident ticket INC-2026-0422 with severity P2 — root cause: RBAC refactor + audit sink filter masked failure. Remediation steps and timeline in ticket.
auditd-bot: New alert rule created: kms.decrypt_denied -> channel #eng-security, severity=high when count>3 in 10m.
devon: One more long-term fix: move KMS decrypt permission to KMS key policy binding instead of relying on SA impersonation where possible, and document the mapping.
anna: Agreed. I'll add the doc to the security runbook and assign owners. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. :heart:
devon: +1 — follow up items assigned. Closing thread once postmortem drafted.
